name: Chokebore
label: AmRep
lede: Chokebore started in Honolulu, signed to Amphetamine Reptile off a demo tape, and ended up spending seven or eight months a year touring Europe, where the crowds were.

eras.title: From Dana Lynn to Chokebore
eras.text: Three friends from Honolulu's punk scene start a band under a name they later say they always hated, and one of them heads to art school in Los Angeles.

years.h: A Honolulu skate crew starts a band called Dana Lynn
years.p: [[Troy von Balthazar|66003585-5be1-4afa-8d37-e7c43743232b]], Jon Kroll and James Kroll meet in Hawaii's punk and skate scenes. The name on the first flyers is one they'd later say they always hated.
years.xp:
Von Balthazar told Flipside in 2000 that the three started playing together about ten years earlier, all of them coming out of different Hawaii punk bands. Two of them had even passed through the same band, Mug, at different times.

Dana Lynn only became Chokebore when a single on Amphetamine Reptile was on the way. Von Balthazar also said he wasn't originally the singer. He learned along the way, and had changed his birth name, Bruno, to Troy at sixteen to escape teasing.

years.h: Art school takes Jon Kroll to Los Angeles
years.p: Kroll goes for graduate study in art in 1991. The band carries on as a trio for about 18 months, six of them in San Francisco.

eras.title: The demo that reached Minneapolis
eras.text: Tom Hazelmyer hears the tape, and within months there's a picture-disc 7-inch, a debut album and a spot on Nirvana's last American shows.

years.h: A demo tape lands at Tom Hazelmyer's Minneapolis label
years.p: [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s Amphetamine Reptile Records signs Chokebore in March 1993 on the strength of the tape alone.
years.xp:
By the band's own account, the trio had gotten back together with Jon Kroll in the winter of 1992 before the tape went north. AmRep followed with the picture-disc 7-inch Nobody / Throats to Hit in May 1993.

Chokebore's quiet-then-sudden dynamics sounded unlike much of the AmRep catalog. The band got filed under sadcore anyway.

years.h: Motionless is cut at AmRep's own studio, catalog number 020
years.p: Engineer Tim McLaughlin records the debut in Minneapolis, and Hazelmyer designs the cover. Johnee Kop plays drums.
years.xp: The album includes Hit Me, a reworking of Rod Stewart's Do Ya Think I'm Sexy? that keeps only the original verses. Coat got a video by David H. Moe on an AmRep video compilation.

yt: Chokebore live at the Jabberjaw, Los Angeles, Oct 10, 1993
years.h: Chokebore, Today Is The Day and Guzzard share a van tour called Clusterfuck
years.p: Three AmRep bands split a fall 1993 US run, after Chokebore had already gone coast to coast with Australia's Cosmic Psychos.
years.xp: The band's biography puts the Clusterfuck run at six weeks. Footage survives of a full Chokebore set at the Jabberjaw in Los Angeles on October 10, 1993, from the same fall.

years.h: Ten shows on the west coast with Nirvana and the Butthole Surfers
years.p: Chokebore opens for [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] on some of the last American dates of [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]]'s band.
years.xp:
Chokebore's own biography describes a ten-show support run with Nirvana and the Butthole Surfers and places it in winter 1994. Wikipedia describes them among the openers on Nirvana's last ten American shows. Dates vary by source.

A French interview also lists Deftones and Tool among the bands Chokebore later opened for.

yt: Spear and Sadavia, live in Germany, 1994
years.h: The European Clusterfuck: one bus, 11 countries
years.p: The same AmRep package plays 30 shows in about five weeks, and Europe starts turning into Chokebore's home audience.
years.xp: Von Balthazar said in 2000 that the band spent seven or eight months of each year in Europe. Wikipedia says Chokebore did better commercially there than at home, especially after Anything Near Water.

eras.title: Bitter, pretty and loud
eras.text: Two albums, a drummer swap and a lot of European highway.

years.h: Biff Sanders records Anything Near Water in Los Angeles
years.p: The second album is made at Motiv in LA, and it's the last one with original drummer Johnee Kop.
years.xp: Sanders engineered and co-produced with the band. A 7-inch, Thin as Clouds, followed the same year. The band's biography says the album earned "insider tip" status, and Vicious Circle reissued it on orange vinyl in 2013 for the band's 20th anniversary.

years.h: Christian Omar Madrigal Izzo takes the drum stool
years.p: Johnee Kop leaves, and Izzo starts touring with the band in 1995.
years.xp: The same year the band played a European run of 51 shows in 15 countries, September to October, from Bergen, Norway to Barcelona, Spain.

yt: A Taste for Bitters, live on French TV, 1997
years.h: A French village hosts the recording of A Taste for Bitters
years.p: The band tracks its third album in spring 1996 at Black Box studio in Noyant-la-Gravoyere with engineer Peter Deimel, in a break from touring Europe.
years.xp: Released October 2, 1996 on AmRep, it was the first record with Izzo on drums. Marcos Siega directed a video for the title track, and the band shared a split 7-inch that year with German band Tocotronic.

years.h: It Could Ruin Your Day gets a Darren Doane video
years.p: The single comes out in 1997, and Doane films the clip.

eras.title: Leaving AmRep, staying on the road
eras.text: The band moves to Boomba in Europe, changes drummers twice and keeps touring through the van years before a long quiet.

yt: Coat and Comeback Thursday, live in France, 1998
years.h: Back to France with a new drummer for Black Black
years.p: Mike Featherson joins for the fourth album, recorded in February 1998 at Black Box and released April 13 through Boomba in Europe.
years.xp:
The US release came September 10, 1999 on Punk in My Vitamins. The band has said the title came from a Japanese chewing gum brand. The CD version adds a 15-minute closing track, The Rest of Your Evening.

Chokebore's site calls it the band's high point.

years.h: Izzo comes back after two and a half years away
years.p: Featherson leaves once the Black Black cycle ends, and Izzo returns to the kit.

years.big: We've eaten so much dirt along the way, that I think now we can eat dirt, and not really feel it as hard.
q: We've eaten so much dirt along the way, that I think now we can eat dirt, and not really feel it as hard.
years.h: Three months in a van, a week at home, then gone again
years.p: Von Balthazar to Flipside, spring 2000, on a schedule that included eighty shows in a row.
years.xp: He also talked about the odd rooms the band had played, Sarajevo and the Arctic Circle among them, since Europe was where Chokebore had its crowd.

years.cap: Troy von Balthazar singing live, April 2001
years.h: Redwood puts out the Strange Lines EP
years.p: After a long stretch of touring and silence, Chokebore is back in the racks in February 2001.

years.h: It's a Miracle arrives on Pale Blue after four years of silence
years.p: Chokebore's fifth album is looser and more personal than what came before.
years.xp: Pale Blue also reissued Motionless and Anything Near Water that year, with new artwork by Jonathan Kroll. The band's site calls the album more mature and less sad than its predecessors.

eras.title: The hiatus, the solo records, the return
eras.text: The band goes on hiatus in 2005, everyone scatters into other projects, and then a European reunion turns into a new EP.

years.src: Chokebore: Wikipedia · Troy von Balthazar: Wikipedia
years.h: Chokebore goes on indefinite hiatus
years.p: Von Balthazar later said some members had children and other commitments, and that being great means giving everything.
years.xp: Von Balthazar started making solo records: home-recorded EPs from 2001 as B. Balthazar, then a deal with French label Olympic Disk and a 2005 debut recorded at Elliott Smith's old studio. Izzo toured with Christian Death 1334, and Jon Kroll began the wordless guitar project A Newborn Riot Of Dreams.

years.cap: Chokebore on an outdoor stage at the Hippodrome d'Evreux, France, June 2010
years.h: A homepage post says Chokebore is getting back together
years.p: On November 18, 2009 the band announces a handful of European shows.

years.cap: Chokebore on the Falls Best tour, December 2011
years.h: Falls Best is the first new Chokebore record in nearly a decade
years.p: The five-track EP comes out October 10, 2011 on Vicious Circle.
years.xp: Vicious Circle opens it with Lawsuit and closes with Awesome. The band toured Europe behind it, including a Paris show at La Machine du Moulin Rouge on October 31, 2011.

years.h: Twenty years on, Vicious Circle reissues the first two albums
years.p: Motionless comes out on white vinyl and Anything Near Water on orange.

eras.title: Back in print
eras.text: Two labels put the old records on vinyl again.

years.h: Black Black goes back on vinyl, twice
years.p: Vicious Circle reissues it in December 2024, and Amphetamine Reptile follows with its own pressing in May 2025.
